newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-BELEAGUERED SPURS CHEERED BY WIN OVER PACERS.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-BELEAGUERED SPURS CHEERED BY WIN OVER PACERS.

text.p: The beleaguered, injury-plagued San Antonio Spurs gave themselves something to feel good about for a change.
Avery Johnson scored 26 points and Vinny Del Negro sparked a late 8-0 run to lead the Spurs to a 102-98 victory over the Indiana Pacers on Saturday.
Del Negro finished with 25 points and Carl Herrera chipped in 21 as the Spurs' five starters scored 93 of the team's 102 points.
Rik Smits scored 25 points and Reggie Miller added 21 for Indiana, losers of three in a row.
Dale Davis, who contributed 20 points and 18 rebounds, put the Pacers ahead 93-92. But Del Negro hit two free throws with 1:23 to play to begin an 8-0 spurt that sealed the win.

"We've had a tough season and this was a nice win," said Del Negro after the Spurs won consecutive games for the first time since January 3. "It's nice to go home with a couple of victories after this long road trip."

The Spurs (15-46), who have been without superstar centre David Robinson and regular starting forward Charles Smith for virtually the entire season, have already lost more games than in the last two seasons combined.
"This season has felt like four seasons," Johnson said. "We needed something good to happen to us."

In Cleveland, Vin Baker had 25 points and 15 rebounds and Glenn Robinson added 20 points and nine rebounds as the Milwaukee Bucks snapped an eight-game losing streak with a 90-82 victory over the Cavaliers.
Sherman Douglas contributed 12 points and seven assists and Johnny Newman chipped in 11 points for the Bucks, who beat The Cavs for just the second time in their last 14 meetings.
Terrell Brandon had 25 points, 10 assists and five steals and Tyrone Hill added 19 and 11 rebounds for Cleveland.
The Cavaliers mounted a late threat as Brandon scored five points in a 7-0 spurt to pull within 76-74. But the Bucks thwarted the rally, scoring 11 of the next 12 points.
In Los Angeles, Joe Dumars scored 23 points and Grant Hill added 19 points to lead the Detroit Pistons to a 91-85 win over the Clippers.
Hill also had 10 rebounds and eight assists and Otis Thorpe added 15 points for the Pistons (45-16), who moved into a tie with idle Miami for the third playoff spot in the Eastern Conference.
Loy Vaught scored 23 points and Rodney Rogers added 17 for the Clippers, who have lost four in a row.
